title: Tax and TDS on IDCW
objectives: State how IDCW is taxed since April 2020 and the TDS threshold.
Explain that TDS is not the final tax, and that reinvestment and transfer are taxed as payouts.
body_md:
Since 1 April 2020, IDCW is taxed in the investor's hands at their slab rate, like other income. Before that, the fund paid a distribution tax and the payout was tax-free for the investor; many clients still remember the old rules. For resident investors, the AMC deducts TDS at 10% when IDCW from that AMC exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year (the threshold was ₹5,000 until March 2025). TDS is not the final tax: it is adjusted when the client files the return. Clients in a higher slab may owe more; those below the taxable limit can claim a refund or submit the declaration forms that allow no deduction, where eligible. IDCW reinvestment and transfer are taxed the same way as a payout. Rules change with Budgets; refer every specific question to the client's CA.

> **Investor takeaway:** Choose IDCW only if you understand that it is your own money, taxed in full, on the fund's timetable.
example: IDCW of ₹12,000 from one AMC in a year: TDS at 10% applies above the ₹10,000 threshold — and the full payout is still reported as income in the return.
say: TDS is not the final tax; it is adjusted in the return.
IDCW reinvestment and transfer are taxed the same way as a payout.
never: TDS on IDCW is the final tax; nothing more is reported.

check.why: At the investor's slab rate. In the investor's hands.

check.q: For residents, TDS on IDCW applies above what yearly amount per AMC?
What happens to TDS deducted on IDCW when the client files their return?
o: Nothing — it is the final tax
It is adjusted; IDCW must still be reported as income
It is refunded automatically to everyone
